parts.text: A student determines the focal length f of a lens. Fig. 3.1 shows the set-up.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • He places the screen at a fixed distance from the illuminated object. • He places the lens between the object and the screen so that the lens is very close to the screen. • He moves the lens slowly away from the screen until a clearly focused image is formed on the screen. • He measures the distance u between the object and the centre of the lens and the distance v between the centre of the lens and the screen. The readings are shown in Table 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 3.1, measure the distance d between the illuminated object and the screen. d = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Fig. 3.1 is drawn 1 / 10th actual size. Calculate the actual distance D between the illuminated object and the screen. D = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate, and record in Table 3.1, the focal length f of the lens using the equation f = uv D . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) • The student keeps the screen at the same fixed distance D from the illuminated object. • He moves the lens slowly away from the screen. The image goes out of focus. • He continues to move the lens slowly away from the screen until another clearly focused image is formed on the screen. • He records the new readings of u and v in Table 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate, and record in Table 3.1 the new value for the focal length f of the lens using the equation f = uv D . [1] Table 3.1 u / cm v / cm f / cm 59.8 20.4 19.8 60.0

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average value f A of the focal length of the lens. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. f A = ................................................... cm [2]

ms.label: 3(d)
ms.text:
one from:
darkened room / brighter lamp
object and lens at same height (above bench)
object and lens and screen perpendicular to the bench
ruler on bench or clamped
mark centre of lens (on holder)
move lens slowly / back and forth (to obtain best image)

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Another student wants to obtain more measurements for u and for v to check the value for the focal length f of the lens. The student moves the screen a distance of 40.0 cm to the right.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the new value for the distance D between the illuminated object and the screen. D = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student moves the lens to a new position which is a distance from the object u = 22.2 cm. He observes the image on the screen and says it is clearly focussed at a distance v = 97.9 cm. Calculate the new value of the focal length f of the lens using f = uv D . f = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(e)(iii)
ms.text:
(expect not in agreement)
too far apart / not close enough / more than 10% difference between values
